item.title: Version 2.7.0
item.description:
Added

  • A widget for the desktop and Notification Centre, in three sizes. Small shows your current or next meeting; medium shows three meetings and large shows seven, each with a Join button. To add it, right-click the desktop, choose Edit Widgets and search for MeetingView.
  • The widget follows the same choices as the menu: your calendars, your event filters, dismissed meetings, and hidden titles.
  • MeetingView has to be running for the widget to stay up to date. If it hasn't run for a day, the widget asks you to open it.

Changed

  • Releases are now checked to start correctly after notarization, before they are published.

item.title: Version 2.6.0
item.description:
Added

  • Leave-by reminders. For a meeting with a location and no meeting link, MeetingView can tell you when it's time to leave, using the travel time from where you are: "Leave by 13:30 to arrive for 14:00. About 25m by car." Turn it on in Preferences → Notifications → Leave-by Reminders, and choose car (the default), on foot or public transport.
  • The reminder needs location access, which MeetingView asks for when you turn it on. Without it, or when Maps can't find the place, the reminder comes a fixed time before the start (15 minutes unless you change it).
  • Open in Maps in the actions of a meeting that has a location and no meeting link. It opens directions from where you are.

Privacy

  • Leave-by reminders are off by default. While they are on, MeetingView sends the meeting's location and your Mac's location to Apple Maps to get the travel time. Nothing else about the meeting is sent.

item.title: Version 2.5.0
item.description:
Added

  • Running late. A meeting's actions now include Running late, with 5, 10 and 15 minutes. It opens an email to the organizer, or to everyone invited, with the meeting's title as the subject and your message written. Nothing is sent until you press Send. Choose who gets it and what it says in Preferences → Notifications. There is also a keyboard shortcut and a "Send Running Late Message" action for Shortcuts and Siri.
  • Urgency colours. The menu-bar title turns orange two minutes before a meeting starts, and red for its first ten minutes if you haven't joined it from MeetingView. Change the timing or turn it off in Preferences → Display & Events → Status bar.
  • Documents. A meeting's details now list the documents linked in its invitation, such as Google Docs, Notion, Figma, Confluence and Microsoft 365 files, and any other web page. Click one to open it. This needs "Show event: details as submenu" turned on.
  • Focus filters. A macOS Focus can now choose which calendars MeetingView shows, and silence its notifications, while that Focus is on. For example, show only your work calendars during Work. Add it in System Settings → Focus → your Focus → Focus Filters → MeetingView. Your usual calendars return when the Focus ends, and the menu says when a filter is on.
  • Morning summary. One notification each morning with the number of meetings, the time they take, the busiest stretch and when the first one starts. Off by default; turn it on and pick the time in Preferences → Notifications.

item.title: Version 2.4.0
item.description:
Added

  • Focus time. Ask your calendar for it, for example "Find me two hours of focus time before Thursday", and MeetingView lists slots of that length that are free of meetings. Each slot has a Block button that adds it to your calendar, and an Undo. MeetingView adds an event only when you click Block, and never changes or removes any other event.
  • Working hours. Preferences → Planning sets the hours and days that free time and focus slots are looked for in. The default is 09:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday.
  • Preferences → Planning also chooses the calendar focus blocks are added to, and their title.
  • A summary of each day under the Today and Tomorrow headers in the menu, when the day has two or more meetings: how many, how long in all, the busiest stretch and any overlaps. Turn it off in Preferences → Display & Events → Menu.
  • Asking what's on a day or a week now starts the answer with the same summary. For a week it names the busiest day.

Changed

  • "Before Thursday", "until Friday" and "by tomorrow" in a question now mean every day up to then, not that day alone.
  • Free time now avoids every meeting in your calendars, including ones you have chosen to hide from the menu.

item.title: Version 2.3.0
item.description:
Added

  • Ask your calendar. Choose Ask Your Calendar… in the menu and type a question in plain language, such as "When am I free tomorrow afternoon?", "What's on Thursday?", "Anything with Sarah this week?" or "Find me a two hour gap this week". MeetingView answers from your calendar, up to two weeks ahead, with a Join button on meetings you can join.
  • Ask runs on your Mac with Apple Intelligence. Your calendar and your questions never leave it.
  • Each answer shows how your question was understood, so you can see when it was misread.
  • A keyboard shortcut for Ask (Preferences → General → Keyboard Shortcuts) and an "Ask Your Calendar" action for Shortcuts and Siri.

Changed

  • MeetingView now requires macOS 26 or later. Ask also needs a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, with it turned on; the rest of the app works without it.

item.title: Version 2.2.1
item.description:
Changed

  • When there is no meeting to show, the menu bar now shows the MeetingView icon in your chosen colour instead of a grey calendar. To keep the calendar icon, set Preferences → Display & Events → Icon to "Calendar".

item.title: Version 2.2.0
item.description:
Changed

  • The MeetingView icon in the menu bar now has the colour you chose for the app icon, and changes as soon as you pick another. It appears when the menu-bar icon is set to "MeetingView" in Preferences → Display & Events, and whenever MeetingView shows its own icon, such as before any calendar is selected.

item.title: Version 2.1.0
item.description:
Added

  • A new app icon, in six colours. Choose yours in Preferences → General → App icon: blue (the default), green, purple, pink, yellow or graphite. Your choice appears in MeetingView's windows, alerts and update prompts. Finder and notifications always show the blue icon.

Changed

  • The "MeetingView" menu-bar icon matches the new app icon.

item.title: Version 2.0.0
item.description:
MeetingView 2.0 is a complete rebuild. It does the same job, with the same settings, on a new foundation.

Added

  • Right-click the menu-bar item to join the current or next meeting straight away.
  • The menu has a join item for the current or next meeting at the top.
  • A long meeting title that doesn't fit in the menu bar now falls back to the icon alone, so the item never disappears.

Changed

  • MeetingView now requires macOS 14 or later.
  • The app's language is chosen in System Settings → General → Language & Region → Applications. Preferences → General has a button that opens it. A language picked in 1.x carries over.

Removed

  • The Advanced tab in Preferences, and with it Shortcut hooks, AppleScript hooks and regex filters.
